# Studienstiftung Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes was originally founded in Dresden in 1925 as a department of the Deutsche Studentenschaft but was dissolved under National Socialism in 1934, subsequently being re-established as a registered association in Cologne in 1948.
The organization offers a general scholarship for bachelor's and master's studies, which provides both financial and academic support, with eligibility tied to the criteria of BAFöG, the German state support system for students. The Studienstiftung seeks exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates based on the principles of "excellence, initiative and responsibility." Admission occurs through multiple channels, including nomination by a school or professor, nomination by an examination board, selection as a winner of a national or federal competition, participation in an assessment test, or nomination by alumni.
